column1: # TITLE: Carbon-ion radiotherapy of human lung cancer

# SUMMARY: Carbon-ion irradiation is an emerging therapeutic option for several tumor entities including lung cancer. Well oxygenated tumor areas compared to a hypoxic environment favor therapeutic photon irradiation efficiency of solid tumors due to increased amounts of DNA damage. The resistance of hypoxic tumor areas towards photon irradiation is enhanced through increased HIF-1 signaling. Here
column2: we compared the effects of oxygen and HIF 1 after photon and carbon-ion irradiation with biological equivalent doses in a human non-small lung cancer model. In hypoxia compared to normoxia
column3: A549 and H1299 cells displayed improved survival after photon irradiation. Knockdown of HIF-1α combined with photon irradiation synergistically delayed tumor growth in vivo. Photon irradiation induced HIF-1α and several of its target genes such as PDK1
column6: and VEGF with subsequent enhanced tumor angiogenesis in vivo
column7: a signaling cascade that was not targeted by carbon-ion irradiation. We present evidence that photons but not carbon-ions induce HIF-1α via mTOR pathway. Importantly
column9: we observed substantial downregulation of HIF-1α and a drastically delayed tumor growth indicating a considerable higher relative biological effectiveness (RBE) than anticipated from the cell survival data. In sum
column10: our results demonstrate that carbon-ions mediate an improved therapeutic response of tumor treatment compared to photon irradiation that is independent of cell oxygenation and HIF-1 signaling.
